title.from: GitHub webhook -> SQS -> EFS git sync worker
title.to: Verify GitHub webhook-triggered tenant sync and Kanbus event

description.from:
## Intent
Implement event-driven Git synchronization from GitHub into EFS-backed tenant repos.

## Scope
- Verify GitHub webhook signatures
- Enqueue sync jobs to SQS
- Worker fetch/reset repo on EFS per tenant
- Detect issue/config changes and publish IoT events

## Definition of Done
- Retry and DLQ behavior works as expected.
- Per-tenant sync lock prevents overlapping sync races.
- CloudWatch alarms are configured for failures and backlog.
- End-to-end webhook-to-event flow is reproducible in test.
description.to:
## Context
This is the verification slice under the Event-driven GitHub integrations for Kanbus initiative. A signed GitHub push webhook can keep a cloud tenant's Git-backed Kanbus data fresh and emit a notification for downstream features. It is useful for changes initiated in GitHub, but it is not needed for the current single-worker Issue Router dispatch path.

## Start with evidence reconciliation
The deployed cloud-backend epic records webhook/sync validation as complete, while this task's older note says signed ingress was blocked on access to the webhook secret. Inspect the existing validation artifacts and deployment/runbook first. Do not rebuild the webhook, queue, worker, or EFS path if the prior evidence already proves them.

## Remaining work
If evidence is incomplete, run one signed test delivery and trace it through signature verification, SQS, the correct tenant's EFS checkout, and the published Kanbus/IoT change event. Confirm duplicate delivery and retry behavior do not create unsafe duplicate effects, and record the precise least-privilege permission needed for the test. If evidence is already complete, link it and close this task.

## Acceptance
- The end-to-end signed-event result is reproducible or existing evidence is linked.
- Tenant isolation, retry/DLQ behavior, and the resulting change notification are accounted for.
- Any missing credential permission is recorded as a precise owner/action, not left as an unexplained blocker.
- Future PR, review, or CI webhook actions are separate scoped issues under the initiative.
